name: Yvonne Daniels
description: Announcer on WYNR (all-Black format, Gordon McLendon ownership) in the early 1960s; hired by WLS in 1973 as its first female air personality; held the overnight shift for nearly eight years; later worked at WVON, WGCI, and WNUA; died 1991 at age 54.

name: Your Love
description: “Your Love” is a 1986 Chicago house song written and first recorded by Chicago singer, songwriter and producer Jamie Principle, who wrote its lyric as a poem for his girlfriend Lisa. Principle's home-recorded demos circulated among Chicago DJs on reel-to-reel tape from the early 1980s, and Frankie Knuckles — then defining the sound of the city's clubs — took the song up, playing his own version at the Power Plant. After a mix by Mark “Hot Rod” Trollan, the small Persona Records gave the song its first public release in April 1986; Trax Records re-released it in 1987 credited to Knuckles, with Principle credited as songwriter, a crediting dispute that shadows the record's history. It charted in the United Kingdom in 1989 and, after Knuckles' death in 2014, re-entered at number 29. In 2026 the Library of Congress selected both Principle's 1986 original and Knuckles' 1987 version for preservation in the National Recording Registry.

name: Young Lords Organization
description: Puerto Rican Chicago organization that began as a Lincoln Park street organization and, under José 'Cha Cha' Jiménez, became a political organization in 1968. It ran free breakfast programs, a daycare center, and free health and dental clinics; fought Lincoln Park gentrification; and on April 4, 1969 co-led the formation of the original Rainbow Coalition with the Illinois Black Panther Party and the Young Patriots.

name: Yeshimabeit Milner
description: Founder/CEO of Data for Black Lives (2017), a movement of scientists and activists using data science for racial justice; originator of the 'Abolish Big Data' call for community control of data.

name: Yearbook (1955 Allen University 'Yellow Jacket')
description: The 1955 'Yellow Jacket' is the yearbook of Allen University, held by the Smithsonian's National Museum of African American History and Culture as object 2017.99.2 and cataloged as public domain. It was published by the Taylor Publishing Company of Dallas, Texas — also the publisher of the second verified exemplar in CultureTechLens's object-biography research, East High School's 1970 'Grey Eagle' (NMAAHC 2018.15.3). A bound volume of campus and class photographs, the yearbook documents the academic and social life of the university in 1955; the companion 'Grey Eagle' preserves handwritten student inscriptions, evidence of yearbooks kept and exchanged as personal records. No advertising pages were documented for either copy. The museum frames such yearbooks as archives affirming Black institutional and school life, and schools as community anchors.

name: Yusef Lateef
description: Yusef Lateef received the NEA Jazz Masters Fellowship in 2010. In CultureTechLens's research he is named on the historic stage roster of Chicago's Jazz Showcase — a roster the project's venue-scout document calls a jazz canon — and his performances there were among the soundboard recordings founder Joe Segal made, with the musicians' consent, across decades at the club: in April 2026, LP sets of 1970s Showcase performances by Lateef, Joe Henderson, Ahmad Jamal, and Mal Waldron were released for Record Store Day. He is cataloged as entry CTL-JAZZ-089 in the CTL-JAZZ-100 dataset of African American jazz artists. Beyond these facts the corpus states no instrument, recording, or biographical detail for him, and none is imported.

name: YOUmedia
description: YOUmedia is a Chicago Public Library teen media space opened in July 2009 at the Harold Washington Library Center, the library system's main branch. The record's cited source, the research brief 'Black Chicago Goes Online' (CTL-RB-TECH-000002 v1.0, 2026-10-09), states that the Chicago Public Library and the Digital Youth Network opened YOUmedia together; that it is a space where teens make media rather than just consume it; and that three branch sites were scheduled to open in June 2011 — a schedule the brief reports, not an outcome it confirms. The Digital Youth Network, the co-founding partner, was started in 2006 by Nichole Pinkard with a $1.6 million MacArthur Foundation grant, bringing digital-media literacy to middle and high school students. The graph record is Provisional, under project TECH-001.

name: Yolanda King
description: Yolanda Denise King was born in Montgomery on November 17, 1955, two weeks before Rosa Parks's arrest launched the bus boycott her father would lead, and she was an infant in the house when it was bombed in January 1956. Her father, Martin Luther King Jr., wrote of explaining to young Yolanda why she could not enter the Funtown amusement park — an early, searing lesson in what segregation meant to a child. She was twelve when her father was assassinated. Rather than live only as a symbol of that loss, King built her own instruments: she earned a degree with honors in theatre and African American studies at Smith College and a master's in theatre at New York University, then used performance as public teaching. She played Rosa Parks in the 1978 television miniseries King, Betty Shabazz in Death of a Prophet, and Medgar Evers's daughter Reena in Ghosts of Mississippi — repeatedly embodying the movement's women and families. Through her company, Higher Ground Productions, and years of lecturing, she carried a message of nonviolence, personal growth, and social change to schools and civic audiences, and served the King Center her mother founded. She died in Santa Monica on May 15, 2007, aged fifty-one, shortly after speaking for stroke awareness. Her flowers honor a daughter who refused to be only an heir: she became an artist-activist in her own voice.

name: Yaya Bey
description: Yaya Bey (born Hidaiyah Bey, August 4, 1990, in Queens, New York City) is an American R&B singer-songwriter, the daughter of Juice Crew rapper Grand Daddy I.U. Writing poetic, unflinching songs about Black womanhood, grief, and self-possession, she first gained notice with The Many Alter-Egos of Trill'eta Brown (2016) and broke through with Madison Tapes (2020). Her Big Dada releases — the EP The Things I Can't Take with Me (2021) and the album Remember Your North Star (2022), which Pitchfork scored 8.6 — made her a central figure in that label's reactivation. Ten Fold (2024), made in the wake of her father's December 2022 death, ranged from the cost of living to self-affirmation; Do It Afraid (2025) and Fidelity (2026) — the subject of CTL Short #47 — followed on the Drink Sum Wtr label.

name: Ysaye Barnwell
aliases: Ysaye Maria Barnwell; Ysaÿe M. Barnwell; Dr. Ysaye M. Barnwell
description: Ysaye Maria Barnwell (born February 28, 1946) is an American singer, composer, arranger, and educator best known for her 34 years as a member of the a cappella ensemble Sweet Honey in the Rock, from 1979 to 2013. Trained first as a speech pathologist, she earned a bachelor's degree in speech pathology from SUNY Geneseo in 1967 and a PhD in speech pathology from the University of Pittsburgh in 1975; she later earned a Master of Science in Public Health in 1981. For ten years she was a professor in the College of Dentistry at Howard University, and she co-founded both the graduate program in speech pathology at Howard and the Jubilee Singers at All Souls Unitarian Church in Washington, D.C. As a singer and composer she appears on more than 25 recordings, wrote music for stage and film, and is widely known for leading communal singing through her “Building a Vocal Community” workshops, bringing African American musical traditions, including ring shouts, hymns, and work songs, to singers of all backgrounds.

name: Yara Shahidi
description: Yara Shahidi, born Yara Sayeh Shahidi on February 10, 2000, in Minneapolis, Minnesota, is an American actress, producer, and activist. Her mother, Keri Salter Shahidi, is of African American and Choctaw heritage; her father, Afshin Shahidi, is an Iranian-born photographer who worked as a principal photographer for Prince. The family moved to California when she was four, and she began acting in commercials at age six. Her film debut came opposite Eddie Murphy in Imagine That (2009). She won an NAACP Image Award for playing Zoey Johnson on ABC's Black-ish (2014–2022) and carried the role into its spin-off Grown-ish (2018–2024) as star and producer, earning three NAACP Image Award nominations for Outstanding Actress in a Comedy Series. Time named her one of its 30 Most Influential Teens of 2016. She graduated from Harvard University in 2022 with a degree in sociology and African American studies, founded the youth-voting initiative Eighteen x 18, co-founded the production company 7th Sun with her mother, and played Tinker Bell in Peter Pan & Wendy (2023).

name: Yo-Yo
description: Yo-Yo (born Yolanda Whitaker on August 4, 1971, in South Central Los Angeles) is the West Coast rapper who made female empowerment her explicit subject while most of the industry treated it as a slogan. A protégé of Ice Cube, she debuted on his AmeriKKKa's Most Wanted (1990), trading verses on "It's a Man's World," then released Make Way for the Motherlode (1991), carried by "You Can't Play with My Yo-Yo." She founded the Intelligent Black Women's Coalition and later the Yo-Yo School of Hip-Hop, turning the message into institutions. On screen she appeared in Boyz n the Hood (1991) and recurred on Martin as Keylolo, the role the CTL Short bills; in 2023 she joined A&E's Hip Hop Treasures as a field collector and played Duchess on Disney's Saturdays. CultureTechLens profiled Yo-Yo in Short #158.

name: YNW Melly
description: YNW Melly, born Jamell Maurice Demons on 1 May 1999 in Gifford, Florida, is an American rapper on 300 Entertainment. He broke through with "Murder on My Mind" (2018), which peaked at No. 14 on the Hot 100 and was certified 4× platinum; the albums I Am You (2018), We All Shine (2019) — including "Mixed Personalities" with Kanye West — and Melly vs. Melvin (2019), released while he was incarcerated, followed, the last reaching No. 8 on the Billboard 200. In February 2019 he was charged with two counts of first-degree murder in the October 2018 deaths of Anthony Williams and Christopher Thomas Jr., and pleaded not guilty. His first trial ended in a mistrial in 2023; bond was denied again in May 2026 and a retrial is scheduled for January 2027, with prosecutors seeking the death penalty, per regional and national reporting.

name: Young Jonn
aliases: John Saviours Udomboso; John Udomboso; The Wicked Producer
description: Young Jonn, born John Saviours Udomboso on 16 February 1995 in Ibadan, Oyo State, Nigeria, to a family from Akwa Ibom State, is a Nigerian producer and recording artist billed as "The Wicked Producer" and "Jiggy." He rose in the mid-2010s as an in-house producer affiliated with Olamide's YBNL Nation, with credits including Lil Kesh's "Gbese" and "Efejoku" and Davido's "Biggest Backside," and was ranked No. 3 on The NET's list of Nigeria's top producers. He signed to Chocolate City Music — sources differ on whether in 2021 or 2022 — and crossed over as an artist with the EP Love Is Not Enough (2022) and the hit "Dada," including a Davido remix. "Xtra Cool" became his first solo No. 1 on Nigeria's Top 100. His debut album Jiggy Forever was released 12 April 2024, and a second album, Blue Disco, followed in November 2025.
